The rand weakened toward 17 per dollar as investors fretted about the stability of South Africa’s coalition government, and expectations of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next month bolstered the dollar.
The South African currency slipped as much as 0.4% to 16.9952 per dollar, the weakest intraday level since April. The rand traded at 16.9576 by 9:35 a.m. in Johannesburg, bringing its decline since nationwide municipal elections on Nov. 4 to more than 3%.

China’s growth weakened across the board in October as investment unexpectedly worsened while consumption and industrial output undershot estimates, in a sign Beijing’s latest stimulus measures have yet to feed through to the economy.
Retail sales rose just 0.4% from a year ago, a sharp slowdown from September and far below the consensus forecast of 0.8% by economists polled by Bloomberg. Industrial output expanded at a slower rate for the first time in three months and grew 4.8% in October.

The Indonesian rupiah fell to a fresh record low, pressured by a stronger dollar amid hawkish Federal Reserve expectations, lingering worries over domestic political stability and a potential market downgrade.
The rupiah dropped as much as 0.4% to 18,271 per dollar on Monday. The currency has weakened about 9% this year to underperform regional peers.

Technology stocks plunged ahead of this week’s earnings from Nvidia Corp. and an expected listing by Anthropic PBC, two events that are likely to influence the near-term course of an increasingly fragile AI trade.
Friday’s selloff in US chipmakers spilled into Asia, with a subgauge of the region’s tech shares tumbling more than 6%, the most intraday since Nov. 6. Futures for the Nasdaq 100 lost 1% while those for the S&P 500 Index dropped 0.5%. European contracts also edged lower, while a broader gauge of Asian shares slumped 2.1%.

By Danial AzharNovember 16, 2026 at 6:52 AM UTCBookmark

YTL Power International shares took a breather Monday after their worst weekly selloff in nearly two years as turmoil surrounding Nvidia Corp. and allegations the Malaysian utility has links to Chinese-connected firms cast a shadow over its artificial intelligence business.
The utility firm’s shares plunged 13% last week, the steepest weekly decline since January 2025, erasing more than 3 billion ringgit ($733 million) in market value. Intensifying scrutiny over Nvidia following Jensen Huang’s ouster as chief executive over reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy, has weighed on YTL.

Asia’s two chip-heavy stock markets came under renewed pressure on Monday, tracking US weakness amid Nvidia Corp.’s turmoil and as investors made room for Anthropic PBC’s much-anticipated share sale.
Taiwan’s benchmark Taiex fell 6%, the most since July 17, dragged by foundry Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and chip designer MediaTek Inc. South Korea’s Kospi gauge slid 3.6% as AI chipmakers SK Hynix Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co. both plunged.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Latin America’s fiercest political rivalry, between Argentina’s Javier Milei and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is playing out in Spain, where an election at the end of the month has become a battle of competing ideologies.
At stake is whether Spanish leader Pedro Sánchez, one of the last Socialists governing in Europe, will pull off the kind of miraculous comeback Lula did last month or whether, after almost a decade in power and numerous comebacks of his own, his time is up.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
A potential sign of consumer stress is catching the attention of UK bank equity analysts: missed gym payments.
The percentage of people failing to pay their gym membership fee has risen for five consecutive months, data compiled by the Office for National Statistics shows. It’s a metric that RBC Capital Markets analyst Benjamin Toms is tracking because he sees it as a potential early warning of stress that could spread to credit-card and mortgage payments, which would put pressure on banks.
